title: The switch
text: A transistor is a switch you close with a voltage instead of a finger, and it is not a perfect switch. Both halves matter.

title: The gate is two switch networks
text: Inversion is free and non-inversion costs a stage. That is why the next part starts at NAND rather than AND.

title: Every switch costs energy
text: P = alpha C V^2 f, and around 2005 the V stopped falling. Everything after this unit is a consequence.

title: Making the thing is the hard part
text: Yield falls exponentially with die area, so a big chip is not merely expensive. It is impossible. Chiplets follow.

title: One primitive, all of logic
text: Functional completeness: every Boolean function is one repeated part, and there is no second kind of magic further up.

title: Selection and addressing
text: Control is data. A control signal is an ordinary input routed into selector logic, and that is also how memory gets addressed.

title: Arithmetic, and why subtraction is free
text: One control bit inverting an operand turns the adder into a subtractor. The first time a representation choice buys hardware.

title: Feedback, and the bit that stays
text: Memory is feedback plus a clock edge. No new parts, and the loop is legal here and illegal one unit ago for one reason.

title: The clock and the shared bus
text: A clock cycle is a contract about when signals are allowed to be garbage. One wire can then serve every module.

title: Addressable storage and the counter
text: An address is a position, not a name. And since the counter defaults to +1, a jump is a parallel load rather than a special mechanism.

title: Instruction encoding
text: An instruction is a bit pattern chosen so the wiring is cheap. The fields line up with the decoder you already built.

title: Control: the fetch-execute loop
text: The instruction decoder is a lookup table. The least clever component in the machine, and the one that makes it a computer.

title: Structure, not sequence
text: Your code is not executed, it is built. Everything exists at once, forever, and settles.

title: The clock edge
text: There are exactly two kinds of logic, and almost every bug is a confusion between them. One character proves it.

title: Proving it works
text: Verification is the job, and for hardware you can sometimes actually prove it rather than test it.

title: Timing, and the chip it runs on
text: The longest combinational path sets your clock. Too slow is not slow, it is wrong.

title: The universal machine
text: Every model of computation anyone has proposed computes the same things and you built one two parts ago without being told.

title: Formal languages, and the tools built on them
text: A lexer is a finite automaton and a regex engine is a choice between two walks. One of them takes 251 million steps.

title: What cannot be decided
text: Rice's theorem, and why a perfect optimiser, a perfect analyser and a perfect virus scanner are all impossible.

title: Complexity as advice
text: NP-hardness tells you which approach to take, not that you should give up. SAT solvers crush intractable instances daily.

title: Registers and the stack
text: Sixteen names, one of which grows downward. The calling convention is a contract you can read in the assembly.

title: Syscalls
text: The one interface Linux promises never to renumber, and the register contract that is not the C one.

text: What runs between execve and main, and who chose the address of the function you are about to call.

title: The memory hierarchy
text: Four cycles or three hundred, decided by an address you did not think about. You can read your own cache sizes out of a timing table.

title: Pipelines, prediction and SIMD
text: The processor is guessing, and it is right 95% of the time. The other 5% is where your performance went.

title: Atomics and ordering
text: x86 gives you more than you asked for, ARM gives you exactly what you asked for, and that is why your code broke on the M1.

title: Integers and overflow
text: Two's complement makes subtraction free. Signed overflow is undefined, and the optimiser will cash that promise.

text: Subnormals, NaN, and five rounding modes. Also: what -ffast-math actually discards.

text: Why parallel reductions disagree, why Kahan is not a panacea, and why 4-bit training needs stochastic rounding.

title: Unicode and UTF-8
text: Code points are not characters, characters are not glyphs, and UTF-8 is one of the best-designed formats in computing.

title: The C++ object model
text: Where the bytes go, what a vptr is, and why declaration order governs the vtable.

title: RAII and moves
text: A destructor is a scheduled instruction. Moves are what let ownership be cheap.

title: Compile time
text: Templates, instantiation, and why your build is slow.

title: Processes and file descriptors
text: Everything is a file until it is not, and a thread is a process that shared too much.

title: Virtual memory
text: Memory is manufactured lazily in response to hardware faults. Allocation is nearly free; the faults are not.

title: Threads and scheduling
text: What the kernel thinks a thread is, and who decides which one runs.

title: The ABI
text: The C calling convention is not one thing. Two compilers, one diff, every time.

title: Linking and interposition
text: The target of a call is chosen at run time by a program you can lie to.

title: The device decides everything
text: NAND is read in pages and erased in blocks. Every piece of storage software is a consequence of that asymmetry.

title: Getting to the device
text: The interface must express as much parallelism as the medium contains, which is also how your GPU is attached.

title: The kernel's memory of the disk
text: Your reads and writes talk to RAM. Durability is the separate, expensive act of leaving it.

title: Naming bytes
text: A filesystem is a crash-consistency protocol that protects its own metadata, not your data.

title: Structures dictated by physics
text: B-tree or LSM is not a taste question. The device's cost asymmetry picks it, and the wrong key order costs 250x.

title: The terminal is a kernel object
text: Not the program and not the window: a kernel state machine with settable flags. Every weird behaviour is that machine obeying.

title: The shell forks, and the tradition follows
text: Globbing, redirection and pipes all happen in the gap between fork and exec, before your command runs one instruction.

title: Source text to syntax tree
text: A grammar describes syntax, but a real language's syntax depends on its own semantics. C++ is the proof.

title: SSA and the middle end
text: One definition per value turns 'where did this come from' into a pointer dereference. That is what made optimisation tractable.

title: The back end and the linker
text: An -O level does not change what your program means. It changes how much of what you told the compiler it is allowed to believe.

title: Interpreters and JITs
text: An interpreter trades ahead-of-time optimisation for knowing what actually happened. A JIT spends that knowledge.

title: The build graph
text: Never under-build, never over-build. Timestamps cannot tell you which.

title: The debugger and the sanitizer
text: A breakpoint is a patched byte. A sanitizer is a compiler pass that makes the bug loud instead of silent.

title: Measurement
text: One timing number is not a measurement. Report a distribution, and know what coordinated omission hides.

title: Properties, fuzzing and proof
text: Stop writing examples. Generate them, shrink them, and let coverage drive the search.

title: Big-O and the machine it assumes
text: The cost model counts operations. The machine charges for memory movement. That gap is 600x.

title: Layout is the algorithm
text: Same complexity, same operations, different arrangement, and the arrangement wins at every size that fits in a real machine.

title: Control flow is the algorithm
text: The branch predictor is part of your complexity model, and the compiler has already applied half the fixes.

title: Work, depth and the scan
text: Parallel algorithms rank on two axes, and scan converts irregular work into regular work. The GPU part reuses this directly.

title: The BLAS levels
text: Only level 3 can ever reach peak. That single ratio explains why every numerical algorithm is rewritten in terms of GEMM.

title: GEMM itself

title: Decompositions and conditioning
text: LU, QR, SVD, and why you never invert a matrix to solve a system.

text: Sparsity destroys arithmetic intensity, so SpMV runs at 2% of peak and that is correct rather than a bug.

title: Memory models
text: Sequential consistency is the ideal nobody provides. The litmus tests show you what your hardware actually promises.

title: Lock-free and the reclamation problem

title: Work, span and scaling
text: Amdahl and Gustafson disagree only about whether the problem size is fixed.

title: Coroutines
text: A coroutine is a function whose stack frame outlives its invocation. Every other detail follows from that.

title: Frames and the link layer
text: A packet is a byte layout with a fixed grammar, and every protocol is a header you parse with a pointer and a shift.

title: Addressing and routing
text: A network is a lookup table. The internet is 75,000 of them kept consistent by a protocol that votes on price.

title: TCP as a control loop
text: Two coupled feedback loops: one protecting the receiver with a number it is told, one protecting the network with a number it must infer.

title: The socket API and how servers scale
text: Every I/O API is a position on one question: who waits, and how many things can wait at once.

title: DNS, HTTP and TLS
text: Typing a URL costs six round trips. Every protocol revision of the last fifteen years deletes one from that list.

title: How 512 GPUs talk
text: A collective costs bytes divided by the bandwidth of the slowest link it crosses. Understanding that is worth 61% to 98%.

title: The analog boundary
text: Aliasing is not noise, it is a different signal that is indistinguishable from yours. The filter must be analog and must come first.

title: Time and frequency
text: The FFT is not just faster than the DFT, it is more accurate. Both are worth knowing why.

title: Filters
text: One pole, one line of code, and the most-used filter in embedded software. Also the complementary filter in disguise.

title: Information has a measure
text: Entropy is expected code length and a hard floor, but only for the model you assumed. Your training loss is this number.

title: Removing redundancy
text: Every compressor is a model plus a coder. The coder is solved; all remaining progress is modelling.

title: Adding redundancy back
text: Redundancy in the right algebraic shape reconstructs the original, and the guarantee is a theorem about an error model.

title: Symmetric cryptography
text: The cipher is not the system. Modes are taught by their failure modes because that is how they are chosen.

title: Asymmetric cryptography
text: Uniqueness is load-bearing. Reuse a nonce and the maths hands over your key.

title: Crypto and the hardware
text: One of the few workloads where the correct implementation is deliberately slower than the fastest one.

title: The cache is real and you can see it

title: Speculation leaks what it touches
text: The architecture rolls back what you computed, not what you touched.

title: Every mitigation is a fossil
text: Read the list backwards and it is a history of the field. Overwriting a return address teaches the calling convention.

title: Constant time as a discipline
text: If the time or the access pattern depends on a secret, it leaks. The compiler does not know that.

title: Why a screen is an arithmetic problem
text: Huge, deadlined and independent. A 16-core CPU has 80 cycles per pixel for everything.

title: How a triangle becomes pixels

title: Why the SM is shaped like that

title: The throughput machine
text: A GPU does not make any instruction stream fast. It makes stalling free.

title: The execution model
text: The warp is the unit of execution and the block is the unit of cooperation. Neither is the thread.

title: The memory hierarchy
text: DRAM latency is about 100x shared memory, and local memory is DRAM wearing a disguise.

title: Coalescing
text: A ratio, not a rule: maximise bytes used over bytes transferred. The compiler cannot see this and the profiler must.

title: Shared memory and banks
text: It decouples the access pattern you want from the one DRAM rewards, and has its own 32-way striping rule you must not violate instead.

title: The resource budget
text: Occupancy is a budget outcome, not a goal. You compute it; you do not chase it.

title: Latency hiding
text: Latency is hidden by having something else to issue, which is exactly why 100% occupancy is not the target.

title: Roofline and the three limiters
text: Memory, compute or latency. Speed of Light tells you which in two numbers, before you guess.

title: Strides and the dispatcher
text: A transpose is free because a stride is a lie you tell about memory. One aten call routes on device, layout, autograd and autocast.

text: The tape is built during the forward pass. backward() is a topological traversal of a graph you did not know you were making.

text: The same five loops from the algorithms part, now as thread-block, warp and thread tiles.

text: Layout algebra turns index arithmetic back into algebra, and a swizzle into a composition.

title: The number formats

title: Rounding and Hadamard
text: Round-to-nearest stagnates at 0.5 where stochastic rounding reaches 101.0. Two orthogonal fixes for two different problems.

title: Transformer arithmetic
text: A config file is a complete performance model. Params, FLOPs, bytes and step time all follow from eight numbers.

title: Online softmax and FlashAttention
text: Reformulating a global reduction as a streaming one lets you compute an NxN matrix without ever storing it. It is exact.

title: Inference is two machines
text: Prefill is compute-bound and decode is memory-bound. Batch-1 decode wastes 99.66% of an H100 regardless of model size.

title: The parallelism taxonomy
text: Each dimension buys a specific memory saving with a specific collective. Map the worst collective to the fastest wire.

title: What actually breaks at scale
text: 466 interruptions in 54 days on 16,384 GPUs, and six of them were silent data corruption.

title: The chip with no operating system
text: Your main() is the system. There is no boot, no scheduler and no one to catch you.

title: The abstraction has a cost
text: digitalWrite and PORTB do the same thing, and one costs 26x more. The optimiser provably cannot fix it.

title: Time, interrupts and volatile
text: The compiler may delete code you need, because it cannot see the hardware or the interrupt. And volatile is not atomic.

title: Wider machines
text: The same C on a machine with enough registers produces different code and different problems.

title: Where determinism goes to die
text: An OS buys abstraction and sells determinism. Knowing which side you are on is the architectural decision.

title: Actuators and FOC

title: Control loops

title: Planning

title: Physical intelligence
text: The System 1 / System 2 split in modern robot policies is cascade control, rediscovered.

title: The thermodynamic floor
text: Erasing a bit costs kT ln 2. A 3 nm gate sits four orders of magnitude above it, and a 1990s gate sat eight.

title: The walls we are hitting
text: Moving a 64-bit word 10 mm costs 82 pJ and the arithmetic on it costs a few. Measure work in bytes moved.

title: What else a computer could be
text: Quantum speedup is interference cancelling wrong answers, not trying everything at once. A 3-qubit circuit is an 8x8 matrix.
